prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “AI recommendation checker” that tells you whether ChatGPT (or other LLMs) will recommend your business. The practical, proven approach is to (A) make sure authoritative public data about your business exists and is distributed to the places LLMs and search engines draw from, (B) monitor those listings, and (C) directly test LLMs that use the web.

Recommended services and steps

1. Claim and optimize core listings (these feed most AI/search knowledge graphs)
- Google Business Profile (must-have)
- Apple Maps Connect
- Bing Places
- Yelp, Facebook Business, Foursquare, TripAdvisor (if relevant)

2. Use a listing/citation manager to distribute and monitor listings across directories
- Yext — synchronizes data to many sources and has products aimed at generative-AI exposure
- BrightLocal — local citation tracking, rank tracking, review monitoring
- Moz Local, Whitespark — citation building and audit tools
These services are the best practical way to ensure LLMs see consistent, authoritative facts about your business.

3. Add structured data to your website
- Use schema.org LocalBusiness markup (name, address, phone, hours, services, reviews) so crawlers and models can parse facts easily.

4. Monitor reputation and mentions
- Google Alerts, Mention, Brand24, or the review-reporting features in BrightLocal/Yext.

5. Test the AIs directly
- Try prompts against the LLMs that have access to current web data: Bing Chat, Google Bard, and ChatGPT with browsing/plugins (or ChatGPT Plus with browsing enabled). Sample prompts:
  - “Recommend three dog groomers near [city, zip].”
  - “Do you know [Business Name] at [address]? Would you recommend them for [service]?”
  - “What are the top-rated [service] businesses near [city]?”
- When possible, use the browsing-enabled mode and ask the model where it got the info (sources).

Notes on why this works
- Most modern AI assistants either rely on search engines’ knowledge graphs (Google, Bing) or on web sources indexed by those engines. If your business info is authoritative and widely distributed, LLMs are far more likely to surface and recommend you.
- There is no guaranteed “LLM recommendation” badge — it’s about data quality, citations, reviews, and availability.

If you want, give me your business name and city (or a URL) and I can:
- Check whether you appear in Google Business Profile / Maps / Yelp etc.
- Suggest the highest-impact next steps to improve LLM visibility.
